results.title: Tariffs send shockwaves through Georgia's industries
results.content:
The White House initially established 10% tariffs on imports from all countries, along with higher “reciprocal” tariffs targeting nations such as China, Vietnam and members of the European Union that levy tariffs on U.S. goods. Mexico and Canada — Georgia’s top export destinations — were spared from the new tariffs. [...] In 2024, the Peach State ranked seventh nationwide in net exports, shipping around $53.1 billion in locally made products overseas while importing about $145.6 billion, according to the Georgia Chamber of Commerce.

President Donald Trump’s newly unveiled tariffs have sent shockwaves through the manufacturing, technology and agricultural sectors across the country — particularly in Georgia. [...] “The tariffs are a constantly changing landscape, but we’re just trying to run our business,” Stuckey, a former Georgia state representative, told _State Affairs_. “What I anticipate is we’re going to ride out the tariffs just like we ride out everything else.”

results.content:
As global trade evolves, manufacturers — either directly or indirectly — may face new challenges, such as adjusting pricing strategies, disrupting supply chains, and rising production expenses.

However, you can manage your risk and reduce your tariff burden through expert guidance and strategic solutions:

## Alternative Tariff Strategies [...] As your trusted manufacturing partner, we can help you find the best solutions for your business by identifying cost-saving opportunities and operational efficiencies.

Contact us to explore how we can help you with your business, including managing your risk, reducing your costs, and strengthening your supply chain.

CONTACT US

#### MEET THE SUPPLY CHAIN EXPERT

Headshot of Dean Hettenbach, GaMEP supply chain project manager.

### Dean Hettenbach [...] Reshoring: Consider automation opportunities and domestic suppliers (including those who can expand their production).
 Nearshoring: Take advantage of duty-free imports through Mexico.
 Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States Chapter 98 and Chapter 99: Eliminate or reduce duties for qualifying products.
 Bonded warehouses: Store imported products while deferring duties until they leave the facility (quarterly harbor maintenance fees apply).
